issue.title: Netty isn't being shut down properly?

repository.name: pushy
repository.description: A Java library for sending APNs (iOS/macOS/Safari) push notifications

issue.body:
This issue requires more investigation, but here is a brief summary:

I have a Java web app running on Apache Tomcat 7.0.47 using JDK 1.7.45.
When you shut down Tomcat, the following errors appear:

SEVERE: The web application [] appears to have started a thread named [globalEventExecutor-1-2] but has failed to stop it. This is very likely to create a memory leak.

I know that the GlobalEventExecutor thread is created by Netty.

When Pushy is being shut down via PushManager.shutdown(), is Netty (and other resources) being shut down properly as well?

body: This one somehow slipped away from my plate.  Let me add a method that waits for the termination of the global executor thread.  Meanwhile - yeah, waiting for a second should work.

issue.title: Lingering `ThreadLocals` after graceful shutdown

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

body:
I've just added `awaitInactivity()` method to `GlobalEventExecutor` and `ThreadDeathWatcher`.  When you shut down your application, now you could do this for example:

``` java
GlobalEventExecutor.INSTANCE.awaitInactivity(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
ThreadDeathWatcher.awaitInactivity(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
```

If there's no activity in your application, it should only take less than 2 seconds until these calls return.

Please let me know if this doesn't work for you.
@jchambers are you going to incorporate these into Pushy's PushManager.shutdown(...) ?

@alan-czajkowski Let's not have this conversation here, since Pushy and Netty are entirely separate projects. I think the most appropriate place to discuss next steps is https://github.com/relayrides/pushy/issues/29.

@trustin Please excuse me if I'm being thick here, but [`ThreadDeathWatcher#awaitInactivity(long, TimeUnit)`](http://netty.io/4.0/api/io/netty/util/ThreadDeathWatcher.html#awaitInactivity%28long, java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit%29) appears to be a non-static method. Is there a specific `ThreadDeathWatcher` instance we should be looking at?

Thanks!
